Call A weakly sign-symmetric, or GKK, when A[α, β]A[β, α] ≥ 0 for every almost principal minor, i.e. every minor whose dispersal #α - #(α ∩ β) equals 1. Call A strict GKK when these inequalities are strict for all almost principal minors. Which GKK matrices can be approximated arbitrarily well by strict GKK matrices? artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$. For index sets $\alpha,\beta\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ of equal cardinality, denote by $A[\alpha,\beta]$ the minor of $A$ with row indices $\alpha$ and column indices $\beta$, and write $A[\alpha]:=A[\alpha,\alpha]$ for principal minors. The dispersal of $A[\alpha,\beta]$ is $\#\alpha-\#(\alpha\cap\beta)$; minors of dispersal $1$ are called almost principal.

Call $A$ a $P$-matrix if $A[\alpha]>0$ for every nonempty $\alpha\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$. Call a $P$-matrix $A$ weakly sign-symmetric (GKK) if
$$A[\alpha,\beta]\,A[\beta,\alpha]\ \ge\ 0$$
for every pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ with $\#\alpha=\#\beta$ and dispersal $1$. Call $A$ strict GKK if the above inequality is strict for every such pair. A $\tau$-matrix is a $P$-matrix whose every principal submatrix $A[\alpha]$ has its spectral radius equal to its largest eigenvalue (equivalently, real and positive, dominating in modulus).

(a) Characterize the closure of the set of strict GKK matrices inside the set of GKK matrices: which GKK matrices can be approximated arbitrarily well (in the standard matrix topology) by strict GKK matrices?

(b) In particular, do there exist unstable GKK $\tau$-matrices (i.e., GKK $\tau$-matrices possessing an eigenvalue with negative real part) that can be approximated arbitrarily well by $\tau$-matrices which are strict GKK?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface the original problem list and Holtz's constructions of unstable GKK τ-matrices, along with a later survey "Theorems and counterexamples on structured matrices" (2005) by Holtz and Schneider. No source located confirms that the approximation problem for strict GKK matrices (or specifically for the unstable τ-matrix examples) has been resolved; the problem appears to remain unresolved, but no definitive recent statement was found.
